question: In the radar example, what is P(airplane present | radar registers)?
answer:
Using the given conditional probabilities:

- Prior probability of a plane: \(P(A)=0.05\) [S5]
- Radar detects a plane when it is present: \(P(B\mid A)=0.99\) [S5]
- Radar registers a false alarm when no plane is present: \(P(B\mid A^{c})=0.10\) [S1]

First compute the overall probability that the radar registers something:
\[P(B)=P(B\mid A)P(A)+P(B\mid A^{c})P(A^{c})
=0.99\times0.05 + 0.10\times0.95
=0.0495 + 0.095 = 0.1445.\]

Then apply Bayes’ rule:
\[P(A\mid B)=\frac{P(B\mid A)P(A)}{P(B)}
=\frac{0.99\times0.05}{0.1445}
\approx 0.3425 \approx 34\% .\]

Thus the probability that an airplane is present given that the radar registers something is about **34 %** [S2].
